Internal Emails Raise Questions Over HR Records for DOGE Operative Leading USAID

Background and Appointment

In March 2025, Secretary of State Marco Rubio appointed 28-year-old Jeremy Lewin to lead the US Agency for International Development (USAID), granting him sweeping powers as deputy administrator of policy and programming and chief operating officer. Lewin, a Harvard Law School graduate and former investment banker, was associated with Elon Musk's Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE). His rise to leadership at the agency quickly drew scrutiny due to his lack of prior background in foreign assistance or diplomacy.

However, internal agency records reviewed by reporting organizations revealed a deeper procedural conflict. Emails show that during a critical three-week period from March 18 to April 4—when Lewin began canceling aid programs and terminating thousands of employees—human resources had no record of him in their employment database, and security was unable to issue him an identification badge.

The Onboarding Disconnect and Legal Debate

According to internal correspondence, White House liaison to USAID Adam Korzeniewski initiated onboarding requests for Lewin days after his appointment powers were delegated. By late March, records show Lewin had not yet accepted a temporary job offer or filed standard pre-employment background screening forms, such as the federal OF-306 document required to consummate an appointment and process security clearance reciprocity.

Legal experts interviewed regarding the situation noted that while Rubio delegated top responsibilities to Lewin using an obscure statutory provision (22 U.S.C. § 2385(b)) typically reserved for emergency-response staff deployments, the failure to complete standard federal onboarding procedures has fueled ongoing litigation. Plaintiffs in active federal lawsuits challenging workforce reductions argue that nonconfirmed leadership actions lack proper statutory backing, potentially exposing unvetted actors to questions of legal authority.

Official Responses and Verification

Jeremy Lewin defended his status, stating to reporters that he operated as a regular government employee with a valid State Department-held security clearance under a dual appointment authorized by the Secretary of State and agency counsel. A White House official confirmed that Lewin submitted required paperwork, pointing to appointment and compensation waivers signed by Rubio on March 18.
